chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, when death approaches the dying one, the Angel of Death binds him, and were it not for that, he would not be calm.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the dying person when death approaches according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the 'binding' (awthaqahu) by the Angel of Death is interpreted by Shia scholars not merely as physical restraint, but as a divine facilitation that stabilizes the soul's transition, preventing the chaos of the final moments. This concept underscores the mercy inherent in the process of death, ensuring the believer remains composed for the critical encounter with the divine. It highlights the interplay between the angelic agent and God's will in managing the soul's departure.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The dying one, when death presents itself to him, the Angel of death ties him down, and had it not been for that, he would not be calm’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
when a person is about to die, the angel of death ties him down; otherwise, he will not calm down.”
